ambiguities.text: The specification states clients 'should retain more' than 255 blocks for reorganization handling but doesn't specify how many.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume clients implement their own retention policies beyond the protocol minimum of 255 blocks, typically 1000+ for mainnet.

ambiguities.text: The system transaction to beacon roots contract uses '30M gas allocation' but it's unclear if this is a hard limit or soft limit.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume this is a fixed gas allocation that cannot be exceeded, as system transactions should have deterministic costs.

ambiguities.text: The term 'valid blob' is used without fully enumerating all validity conditions in one place.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume 'valid blob' means: correct KZG commitment (version 0x01), correct format, within MAX_BLOB_GAS_PER_BLOCK (786,432), and proper versioned hash structure.

implicit_assumptions.description: Beacon chain withdrawal data is trusted and not validated by the execution layer beyond format checks.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Malicious consensus layer could credit arbitrary balances, leading to inflation or theft.

implicit_assumptions.description: Attackers cannot forge valid KZG commitments without knowing the underlying blob data.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Blob commitment forgery would allow inclusion of arbitrary data without proper verification.

implicit_assumptions.description: The blob gas market operates efficiently with the exponential pricing formula preventing sustained spam.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Blob gas pricing could be manipulated to either overprice or underprice blob space, affecting L2 economics.

implicit_assumptions.description: Gas refunds capped at 20% of consumed gas prevents refund-based attacks.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Higher refund caps could enable gas token exploits or other economic attacks.
